name: dsh-vim
description: Vim-style keyboard scrolling (d = down, e = up) for whichever pane the pointer is over — the conversation or the sidebar — a message box that never takes focus on its own, a choice of what a bare Enter does in the composer (sends, breaks the line, does nothing, or sends on a double Enter — Ctrl/Cmd+Enter always sends), a stepper for the reasoning level (q), a picker for the model you pick yourself (w: a small window listing each model with all of its reasoning levels, d / e between models, Tab between levels, w again to switch), plus a task window (f) that answers what is waiting on you before where things live: a block for everything whose ball is in your court (an approval, a plan review, a question, or a run you have not looked at yet) ordered longest-waiting first, a dimmed block for turns in flight, then the last three hours in plain time order (measured across the whole pool, so a run in flight still counts as activity; when the window is genuinely empty the block says Earlier rather than Recent and falls back to the newest batch) — a folder is a label on each row rather than a container around rows, so a busy folder can no longer starve a quiet one out of the list; the attention blocks are read off the whole pool so a debt older than the recency window cannot hide behind the More seat, each row is listed once, and the headline says so in words when nothing needs you; the window opens on the first thing waiting on you so dealing with one row makes the next press land on the next, a running turn's clock counts in whole minutes and stays quiet under the first one, each row leads with its state chip and then the folder and name, so the eye reads what it is doing before it reads which conversation, the just-finished chip pulses once when the window opens so the eye lands on it, and the More seat can be walked onto and confirmed with d / e and the open key — a click outside either window closes it, Escape still does, and the click itself still reaches the page
